extracted.intended_audience: judges, patent examiners, patent attorneys, and legal scholars focused on patent law
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating patent quality via doctrinal levers
extracted.subtask_description: Using the article's doctrinal 'policy levers' to evaluate the quality of patent applications and grants and to calibrate prosecution to industry-specific standards (software, biotech, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, etc.). Emphasizes how doctrinal choices (PHOSITA, enablement, written description, eligibility, inequitable conduct, DOE) function as quality controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person Having Ordinary Skill in the Art (PHOSITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothetical PHOSITA's skill level affects nearly every patentability standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality implications: Low-PHOSITA fields (some software, business methods): nearly any combination is patentable and quality requires examiner caution about over-grant. High-PHOSITA fields (biotechnology, pharmaceuticals): obviousness bar is high and quality requires careful prior art analysis. A patent's quality depends on whether the applicant accurately characterized the relevant skill level. Mischaracterized PHOSITA (e.g., portraying biotechnology as low-skill) is a quality defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement (Scope of Disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: How much must the specification teach to support the claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry-specific standards: Pharmaceuticals: single working example often supports claims to closely related compounds. Biotechnology: following Amgen v. Sanofi, structural genus claims require full-scope enablement. Software: functional claiming widely accepted; structural detail rarely required. Mechanical: drawings and one embodiment usually sufficient. Quality marker: Are the disclosed embodiments representative of the claimed scope under the relevant industry standard?

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the specification show the inventor 'possessed' the claimed invention at filing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality marker: Continuation claims drafted years after filing should be scrutinized for whether the original specification supports the new claim language. Late-added genus claims or claims targeting competitor products are red flags indicating weak written description support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of Equivalents (DOE) and Reverse DOE
rubrics_metrics.description: Court-applied scope-modulating tools that expand or contract claim scope beyond literal claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality implications: Pioneer patents claim broad equivalents reach; quality requires that pioneer status be genuine. Improvement patents are vulnerable to reverse DOE, so quality requires that the patent represent a substantial advance over the prior art. Use of DOE should be assessed in light of patent's role (pioneer vs improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-Matter Eligibility (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mayo/Alice framework dramatically affects eligibility for software, biotech, diagnostics, and related claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality markers: Software claims that recite generic computer implementation of an abstract idea are low quality (Alice-vulnerable). Diagnostic claims that recite a natural correlation plus conventional steps are low quality (Mayo-vulnerable). High-quality eligibility-sensitive claims include specific technical implementations or non-conventional combinations that avoid abstract-idea/nature-based rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to disclose material prior art known to the applicant can render the patent unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality markers: Robust Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) submissions with citations from international searches; co-pending applications cross-disclosed; absence of a pattern of selective non-disclosure of the inventor's own prior publications. Patterns of selective withholding of material references are a critical quality defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software industry calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry-specific calibration for software: lower written description bar and widespread functional claiming, but vulnerability under eligibility doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality requires technical specificity to survive Alice; quality marker: claims tied to a particular technical improvement (not merely an abstract result). Even with a lower written-description bar, claims should be drafted to show concrete technical implementation details to avoid eligibility rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnology industry calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnology requires a high enablement and written description bar, especially for structural/genus claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality marker: Representative species supporting genus claims and disclosure of structural-functional correlation. Following cases like Amgen v. Sanofi, broad structural genus claims need full-scope enablement — failure to provide representative embodiments or structure/function linkage is a quality defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceuticals industry calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmaceutical patents have distinct enablement/written-description/utility concerns; single working examples may support close compound claims but method claims face eligibility scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality marker: Compound claims with strong structural support are high quality. Method-of-treatment claims face evolving eligibility issues; supporting pharmacological data and demonstrated utility strengthen quality and reduce vulnerability to challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiconductors industry calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Semiconductor patents confront cumulative-technology concerns and therefore require claim scope that permits design-around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality requires defined scope that permits design-around and avoids overbroad, performance-only claiming. Quality marker: claims tied to specific processes or structures rather than generic 'improved performance' language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: Identify technological regime (industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any patent, first evaluate whether the application correctly identifies the technological regime (industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application misidentifies its industry, the chosen doctrinal calibrations (PHOSITA, enablement expectations, written-description norms, eligibility risks) will be misapplied and weaken the patent. Look for explicit characterization of industry and whether claimed subject matter fits that regime's typical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: PHOSITA skill-level calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the PHOSITA skill level is appropriately calibrated for the technological regime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check prosecution and specification language for assertions about routine skill, required background knowledge, and whether the claim drafting assumes a low- or high-skilled PHOSITA. Mischaracterization is a quality defect (e.g., treating biotech as low-skill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: Enablement disclosure meets industry-specific bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the enablement disclosure satisfies the industry-specific enablement standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the specification's embodiments and examples to the enablement expectations for the relevant field (e.g., representative species for biotech, working examples for pharma, implementation details for software). Lack of representative embodiments relative to claimed breadth indicates poor quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: Claim breadth proportionate to written-description standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether claim breadth is proportionate to the written-description standard applicable in the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large genus claims must be supported by disclosure that shows possession across the breadth claimed. Scrutinize continuation or broadened claims added years after filing for insufficient written-description support or 'targeting competitors' red flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: Anticipate eligibility challenges relevant to field
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the application anticipates subject-matter eligibility challenges that commonly arise in its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For software, watch for claims that merely recite abstract ideas implemented on generic computers. For diagnostics, watch for claims that merely recite natural correlations plus conventional steps. High-quality drafting will include technical implementation details or inventive concept to mitigate Mayo/Alice risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative test: Prosecution history reflects awareness of industry-specific case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the prosecution history demonstrates awareness of and responses to industry-specific case law and prior-art issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality prosecution will cite relevant case law, disclose and distinguish material prior art, make appropriate IDS submissions, and show consideration of eligibility decisions and how claim language was adapted accordingly. Absence of such awareness suggests poor lever-calibration and weaker patents.
